extracted.intended_audience: NeurIPS authors, conference organizers, and researchers studying LLMs in peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Verifying that NeurIPS 2024 conference submissions meet the NeurIPS Author Checklist questions and related submission standards (claims, reproducibility, ethics, data/code licensing, human subjects, etc.). Also covers how an LLM-based assistant should evaluate and report on checklist answers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Do the main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checklist expects matching and precise claims across abstract and introduction; LLM feedback examples emphasize consistency, precision, referencing appendices, and ensuring the contributions section clearly demarcates claims. Actionable feedback: match abstract and intro, avoid overstating, reference supporting sections/appendices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the paper discuss the limitations of the work performed by the authors?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should explicitly discuss limitations; LLM feedback commonly asks for clearer discussion of limitations and suggests adding mitigation strategies or caveats. The assistant often flags missing or shallow limitation sections and suggests where to add them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory Assumptions and Proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: For each theoretical result, does the paper provide the full set of assumptions and a complete (and correct) proof?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the paper contains theory, the checklist requires the full set of assumptions and complete, correct proofs. LLM reviewers may request explicit assumptions behind statistical models even when formal theorems are not present; actionable guidance includes outlining assumptions, providing proofs or pointing to appendices, and clarifying applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental Result Reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the paper fully disclose all the information needed to reproduce the main experimental results of the paper to the extent that it affects the main claims and/or conclusions of the paper (regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect disclosure of all information that affects main claims: data splits, hyperparameters, training details, random seeds, preprocessing, evaluation scripts. LLM feedback often requests section pointers or appendix references and may suggest adding reproducibility checklists or more explicit instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access to data and code
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the paper provide open access to the data and code, with sufficient instructions to faithfully reproduce the main experimental results, as described in supplemental material?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should provide access to code/data and clear instructions for reproducing results (installation, dataset download links, exact commands). LLM reviews check for presence of links, reproduction instructions, and may ask for additional documentation or exact locations in the paper/appendices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental Setting/Details
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the paper specify all the training and test details (e.g., data splits, hyperparameters, how they were chosen, type of optimizer, etc.) necessary to understand the results?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include optimizer config, learning rates, hyperparameter selection methodology, data splits, preprocessing, implementation details. LLM feedback examples show granular suggestions (optimizer configuration details, hyperparameter values, how chosen) and encourage pointing to exact sections/appendices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiment Statistical Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the paper report error bars suitably and correctly defined or other appropriate information about the statistical significance of the experiments?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report error bars, confidence intervals, number of trials, statistical tests where appropriate; LLM reviewers flag missing or improperly defined error bars and recommend correct definitions and presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiments Compute Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: For each experiment, does the paper provide sufficient information on the computer resources (type of compute workers, memory, time of execution) needed to reproduce the experiments?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report compute type (GPUs/TPUs/CPUs), wall-clock runtime, memory, number of machines, and any special hardware. LLM feedback often asks for explicit compute/resource counts and execution time to aid reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code Of Ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the research conducted in the paper conform, in every respect, with the NeurIPS Code of Ethics (https://neurips.cc/public/EthicsGuidelines)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should ensure compliance with NeurIPS Code of Ethics and point to where conformity is discussed. LLMs can flag ethical concerns, misinterpretations, or missing considerations (e.g., anonymity, misuse potential) and recommend clarifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader Impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the paper discuss both potential positive societal impacts and negative societal impacts of the work performed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checklist explicitly requires discussing both positive and negative societal impacts. LLM reviewers frequently ask authors to expand societal impact sections to include negative impacts, mitigation strategies, references to related work, and explicit mention in contributions or dedicated sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the paper describe safeguards that have been put in place for responsible release of data or models that have a high risk for misuse (e.g., pretrained language models, image generators, or scraped datasets)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond licensing, authors should describe safeguards (access controls, usage guidelines, monitoring, mitigations). LLM feedback often requests details beyond licensing, like control mechanisms, recommended usage, or access restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licenses for existing assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the creators or original owners of assets (e.g., code, data, models), used in the paper, properly credited and are the license and terms of use explicitly mentioned and properly respected?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checklist expects explicit attribution and license statements for all third-party assets. LLM reviewers check for explicit citations, appendix license listings, links to licenses, and compatibility of combined licenses; they may request verification or contacting owners if unclear.

rubrics_metrics.name: New Assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Are new assets introduced in the paper well documented and is the documentation provided alongside the assets?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New datasets/models should be accompanied by documentation (datasheets, metadata files), website or repository, and pointers in the paper/appendices. LLM feedback asks authors to reference specific sections, provide preprocessing steps, documentation links, and anonymize URLs if required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crowdsourcing and Research with Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: For crowdsourcing experiments and research with human subjects, does the paper include the full text of instructions given to participants and screenshots, if applicable, as well as details about compensation (if any)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicable, include full instructions, screenshots, compensation details, recruitment methods, and submit these in appendices. LLMs will flag absence or vagueness and advise including full text and documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Review Board (IRB) Approvals or Equivalent for Research with Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the paper describe potential risks incurred by study participants, whether such risks were disclosed to the subjects, and whether Institutional Review Board (IRB) approvals (or an equivalent approval/review based on the requirements of your country or institution) were obtained?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If human subjects are involved, describe risks, disclosures to participants, and provide IRB/ethics approvals or equivalent. LLM feedback asks for explicit statements and documentation; if N/A, authors should state why (e.g., no human subjects).

rubrics_metrics.name: Author checklist response format and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must answer each checklist question with “Yes,” “No,” or “NA” (Not Applicable) along with a justification for their answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justifications should point to specific sections or appendices in the paper; be explicit and precise. The Assistant used these answers plus the paper to evaluate consistency. LLM reviewers suggested amendments when justifications were vague or failed to reference paper sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM scoring scheme
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign Score=1 for no issues, Score=0.5 for minor improvements, and Score=0 for critical issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In practice the study asked the LLM to return a separate score (on its own line) at the end of the review. The authors instructed 'use 0 score sparingly' and for UI combined 0 and 0.5 into a single 'needs improvement' category (orange/red).

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM feedback style and verbosity guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide itemized, actionable feedback focusing on significant improvements and clear examples for Yes/No/NA responses; avoid mixing the review with the score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt engineering found step-by-step instructions, 'itemized, actionable feedback', and 'focus on significant improvements' improved performance. LLMs were advised to keep feedback concise, return score on separate line, provide examples, and avoid overly strict or excessively verbose responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Per-question independent processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat each checklist item as an individual task: one API call per question, with the question, author's answer and justification, and the paper and appendices provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This design isolates evaluation per question and allows targeted feedback. The pipeline aggregated per-question outputs into a combined HTML result. Authors were warned that external links were not considered by the assistant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper processing limits
rubrics_metrics.description: For papers exceeding 35 pages (or ~15,000 words), process only the first 15,000 words and notify authors with a warning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LLM processing truncated long papers to the first 15,000 words; authors were informed. LLMs were observed to miss content beyond this limit; the assistant flagged long papers accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and parsing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers must be formatted per NeurIPS’24 call for papers; the PDF-to-text parser must correctly extract checklist and paper sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The deployment encountered parsing issues (subsections/titles, spacing, ligatures like 'fi'/'fl', incomplete checklists). Authors should ensure proper formatting to avoid parser failures; the assistant did not consider external links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality, anonymity, and consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors could retain anonymity and submissions and LLM outputs were kept confidential and not accessible to NeurIPS reviewers; participants provided informed consent; papers were sent to an LLM API under the API provider's confidentiality terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should be aware that sending data to external LLM APIs entails abiding by the provider's confidentiality terms. The study required informed consent and allowed anonymous registration. The assistant's outputs were restricted to authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calibration of strictness and fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: LLM evaluators should be calibrated to avoid excessive strictness, vagueness, and verbosity; use conservative application of low scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prompt instructed 'use 0 score sparingly' and to 'provide itemized, actionable feedback' and 'focus on significant improvements.' Authors reported LLMs sometimes being too strict or too generic; calibration and prompt tweaks were used to mitigate this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency and variance checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Test whether variation of output scores for multiple runs on the same input is comparable to variation across papers; consistency is expected (lower within-paper variance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study ran repeated evaluations and found within-paper variance significantly lower than across-paper variance for all but the ethics question. LLM-based systems should be checked for unstable outputs across identical inputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vulnerability to adversarial manipulation / fabricated justifications
rubrics_metrics.description: The LLM-based assistant can be manipulated by adversarial authors or AI-assisted re-writing of justifications to make the assistant more lenient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study shows susceptibility to fabricated justifications; systems should be designed with awareness of gaming risks and consider cross-checks, provenance, or human oversight to detect fabricated or misleading justifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation and presentation of LLM responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine per-question LLM responses into a human-readable formatted result (HTML) using color coding (e.g., green = no concerns, orange = needs improvement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The deployment used green for 'no significant concerns' and orange for 'needs improvement'; authors were encouraged to review orange feedback carefully and validate identified issues. The UI combined 0 and 0.5 into a single 'needs improvement' visualization to avoid over-interpretation of severity differences.
